_meta.note: Shared question bank: every nation answers the same questions, in a random order for each nation. Questions unlock by turn. Nations take them one at a time against the clock (quiz_seconds). The stake of each question is random (quiz.stake_min..stake_max in scenario_config.json, average 5); a correct answer earns it and a wrong answer or running out of time loses the same amount of the question's reward_resource, and the question is locked. 'tier' (standard or hard) only says how detailed the question is. Every answer must be stated in the Spireopedia article named in 'article'.

questions.question: What does “AC” stand for in the Continent’s calendar?
questions.explanation: Years are counted from the Great Convergence, the tectonic upheaval three centuries ago.

questions.question: Roughly how long did the Dark Decades of aftershocks and ash-darkened skies last?
questions.explanation: The Convergence itself lasted nine days; the Dark Decades of aftershocks followed for about forty years.

questions.question: In which region does Convergence silt let Alchemical Grain germinate twice as fast?
questions.explanation: The silt plains around the Spire plateaus are the Continent’s breadbasket.

questions.question: How do Sylvan Vault-Wardens keep grain from rotting for decades?
options: They freeze it in mountain glaciers
They seal it in sun marble jars
They bind it with mycorrhizal fungal threads in root-vaults
questions.explanation: Fungal threads in the root-vaults draw off the moisture that breeds rot.

questions.question: What provides the fibre for Echo Silk?
options: Cocoons of luminescent moths in the Whispering Straits
Flax grown on the Solar Plateau
questions.explanation: The moths nest only in the sea-caves of the Whispering Straits.

questions.question: Why do Aquilan ships use rowed, shallow-draft galleys on the Sea of Glass?
options: Sails were banned by the Spire Accords
The sea has almost no wind or current
The water is too shallow for any keel
questions.explanation: The Sea of Glass is mirror-calm: there is no wind to sail by and no current to ride.

questions.question: How many Aether Cores must a nation hold to unlock technological efficiency?
questions.explanation: At 75 or more active cores, a nation’s population consumes a quarter less grain.

questions.question: What does the Two-Sponsor Rule require?
options: Every nation must send two delegates
A motion needs at least two co-sponsoring nations before it can be voted on
Two nations must object to block a motion
questions.explanation: Unsponsored motions die on the floor.

questions.question: Who administers the Neutral Spire?
options: The Archivists, who renounce all national loyalty
questions.explanation: Archivists keep the minutes, count the votes and maintain the Spire Archive.

questions.question: Which nation has only a single base vote in the Assembly?
questions.explanation: Umbra’s base strength is a single vote, which it uses with extreme precision.

questions.question: Which founding agreement created the Sylvan Concordat in 12 AC?
questions.explanation: Nine clan elders swore at the Hearthroot that no clan would let another starve while any vault stood full.

questions.question: Who drew the first solid aether crystal out of the Mistveil Chasm in 31 AC?
questions.explanation: Vorn lowered a basalt crucible on a chain into the vapour.

questions.question: Who holds power in Iron Val-Khor?
options: The Council of Nine, one delegate per Forge Collective
questions.explanation: Delegates are chosen by journeymen vote.

questions.question: What sparked the Ember Riots of 203 AC?
options: The Collectives cut bread rations to fill an order for cores
questions.explanation: Afterwards the Charter guaranteed every foundry-town a grain allocation, the root of Val-Khor’s dependence on Sylvan grain.

questions.question: Who founded the Solaris Ascendancy in 94 AC?
questions.explanation: Sunmaker proclaimed the Mandate of the Sun.

questions.question: What did the Lantern Edict of 119 AC do?
options: It lit the Plenary Hall for night sessions
It banned the export of Echo Silk
It banned unlicensed aether-study and expelled those who refused
questions.explanation: The exiles walked into the Abyssal Rift and founded the Umbral Enclave.

questions.question: How is power divided in the Umbral Enclave?
options: Among Seven Veils, councils that each know only part of every decision
questions.explanation: The founders, remembering the Lantern Edict, made sure no single authority could rule.

questions.question: Who discovered the silk moths that made Aquila rich?
questions.explanation: In 70 AC Ostrel traced the shimmering cocoons in the sea-caves of the Straits.

questions.question: How are votes weighted on Aquila’s Ledger Council?
options: By the size of each house’s fleet
By the taxes each merchant house has paid
questions.explanation: Critics call it an oligarchy; supporters call it honesty.

questions.question: Whom is the Aethelgard Dominion named after?
options: Aethel Garrowmere, who united forty hill-lords
questions.explanation: She gathered the hill-lords to swear the Oath of the Steppe in 33 AC.

questions.question: What must a young Aethelgard knight complete to earn a place at court?
options: A pilgrimage to the Neutral Spire
The Long Watch: a winter alone on a frontier tower
A year of service on an Aquilan galley
questions.explanation: Places at court are earned, not inherited alone.

questions.question: Which two nations fought the Salt War (141–149 AC)?
questions.explanation: It was fought over tolls on salt-ships in the Whispering Straits.

questions.question: How did Aquila win the Salt War?
options: Solaris sent troops to defend it
It closed every League port to Aethelgard until its granaries ran dry
questions.explanation: Within eight months Aethelgard’s army was starving.

questions.question: Where was the treaty that ended the Salt War signed?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Brinegate (149 AC) led directly to the Spire Accords.

questions.question: Which nation sold intelligence to both sides in the Salt War?
questions.explanation: Umbra calls it the rational course for a small state; neither side has fully forgiven it.

questions.question: What was the Midnight Tariff of 149 AC?
options: A grain tariff imposed by one delegate acting alone in a late-night session
A toll on ships crossing the Straits at night
A curfew on trade during the Salt War
A tax on lamps in Lanternfall
questions.explanation: It caused a famine in two provinces and led to the Two-Sponsor Rule.

questions.question: Which nation’s diplomats proposed building a neutral place for talks after the Salt War?
questions.explanation: The Spire Accords were largely a Solaris design, and Solaris has chaired the Plenary ever since.

questions.question: What caused the famine known as the Winter of Open Silos (188 AC)?
options: A tsunami on the Sea of Glass
questions.explanation: A rust-coloured spore turned ripe grain to powder in a single night.

questions.question: Who escorted Sylvan grain convoys during the Winter of Open Silos?
questions.explanation: Aethelgard still cites this whenever its military budget is questioned.

questions.question: What reform followed the Cinder Night of 241 AC?
options: A ban on all aether mining
Safety wardens answerable to the workers, not the managers
questions.explanation: Val-Khor also invited foreign observers into its foundries for the first time.

questions.question: Under the Founders’ Charter, what extra privilege goes to the wealthiest realm?
questions.explanation: The rule was drafted by Aquila’s merchants and has been criticised ever since.

questions.question: In what year does the Summit of Realms convene?
questions.explanation: 298 AC saw the last full harvest; 303 AC the Failed Harvest; the Summit opens in 304 AC.

questions.question: By most estimates, what share of the Continent’s inhabitants died of famine and plague in the Dark Decades?
questions.explanation: Famine and plague killed, by most estimates, two in every three inhabitants.

questions.question: Which three things did the Convergence leave behind that shaped every later age?
options: Obsidian plateaus, sun marble and salt flats
Silt-rich lowlands, raw aether and the memory of scarcity
Fertile silt, volcanic glass and a standing army
Raw aether, silk moths and the Spire
questions.explanation: Fertile silt, raw aether venting from the chasms, and the memory of scarcity.

questions.question: What may a Sylvan Vault-Warden not own?
questions.explanation: “The keeper must not be the eater”: a Warden may not own farmland.

questions.question: Where did the elders of nine clans swear the Pact of Roots in 12 AC?
options: At a ring of standing stones
At a hollow oak called the Hearthroot
questions.explanation: They met at a hollow oak called the Hearthroot.

questions.question: What did the smith Hadrek Vorn lower into the Mistveil vapour in 31 AC?
options: A basalt crucible on a chain
A cooled suit with a lantern
questions.explanation: He lowered a basalt crucible on a chain and drew up the first solid crystal of aether.

questions.question: How many delegates sit in the Solaris Senate of Terraces?
questions.explanation: The Senate of Terraces has 120 delegates elected by the city guilds.

questions.question: Roughly how many exiles walked into the Abyssal Rift after the Lantern Edict?
questions.explanation: Around four thousand scholars, smiths and dissidents.

questions.question: How many islands’ harbour-masters signed the Compact of Harbours in 57 AC?
questions.explanation: The harbour-masters of eleven islands.

questions.question: How many citadels guard the steppe ridgeline?
questions.explanation: A chain of seventeen citadels, each commanded by a hereditary Warden.

questions.question: How many galleries spiral up to the Plenary Hall of the Neutral Spire?
questions.explanation: A spiral of six galleries, one in the style of each nation.

questions.question: What does the fourth provision of the Founders’ Charter require?
options: That the Spire is never garrisoned
That every nation sends two delegates
That the wealthiest realm chairs the Plenary
An emergency Assembly session whenever a nation faces famine
questions.explanation: The Charter requires an emergency session whenever a nation faces famine.

questions.question: Who drafted the rule that gives one extra Assembly vote to the wealthiest realm?
questions.explanation: The rule was drafted by the merchants of Aquila and criticised ever since.

questions.question: Who led Aethelgard’s expeditionary force against the Straits in 141 AC?
questions.explanation: High Marshal Corvane Brask.

questions.question: How long did Aquila’s port closure take to empty Aethelgard’s granaries?
questions.explanation: Within eight months the Dominion’s granaries were empty.

questions.question: By how long did Umbra’s intelligence sales to both sides prolong the war?
questions.explanation: They prolonged the war by almost two years.

questions.question: What did Sylvan’s Vault-Wardens decide in 188 AC?
options: To sell grain at cost to the highest bidder
To distribute grain free to every nation, against their treasurers’ advice
To feed only the northern nations
To wait until the Spire ordered it
questions.explanation: They voted, against the advice of their treasurers, to distribute their reserves to every nation without payment.

questions.question: How did the Vault-Wardens stop the Alchemical Rust at the Lowlands’ borders?
options: They burned a firebreak a hundred miles long
They bound the border crops with fungal threads
questions.explanation: They burned a firebreak a hundred miles long.

questions.question: Roughly how many people died in the weeks after the Cinder Night?
questions.explanation: Over nine thousand people died.

questions.question: What did Val-Khor do for the first and only time after the Cinder Night?
options: Invited foreign observers into its foundries
questions.explanation: It invited foreign observers into its foundries.

questions.question: What is punishable by exile under Aquilan law?
options: Selling silk below the ledger price
questions.explanation: The export of unspun cocoons is punishable by exile.

questions.question: Which year saw the last fully successful harvest before the Summit?
questions.explanation: 298 AC was the last fully successful harvest; 303 AC was the failed one.

questions.question: In what year was the Neutral Spire completed?
questions.explanation: Building began in 150 AC and was completed in 163 AC.

questions.question: After the Ember Riots of 203 AC, what did the rewritten Charter guarantee every foundry-town?
options: A seat on the Council of Nine
A share of the Mistveil cores
questions.explanation: A grain allocation, the root of Val-Khor’s dependence on Sylvan grain.

questions.question: What is the largest annual gathering on the Continent?
options: The Festival of the Long Noon
The harvest oath of the Hearthroot
questions.explanation: The Solaris Festival of the Long Noon.

questions.question: What is the guiding rule of Umbral foreign policy about Assembly votes?
options: No rival should ever hold three or more votes
No two rivals may vote together
Umbra should always hold three votes
questions.explanation: No rival should ever hold three or more Assembly votes.

questions.question: What lasting conviction did the defeat at Brinegate leave in Aethelgard?
options: That it must never field a navy
That it must never again depend on others for food or fuel
That it must never trade with Aquila
questions.explanation: The Dominion must never again be dependent on others for food or fuel.

questions.question: What is the foundation of Umbra’s economy?
options: Synthesising aether from the mineral its walls weep
questions.explanation: The dark mineral that seeps from the Rift’s walls can be synthesised into aether.

questions.question: Whose knowledge of the sea-lanes through the reefs is a guild secret?
questions.explanation: Pilots memorise the sea-lanes, and their knowledge is a guild secret.

questions.question: How does Solaris cope with having little rain?
options: Imported grain and cisterns that collect winter snow
Desalination on the Sea of Glass
questions.explanation: It depends on imported grain and on underground cisterns that collect the winter snow.

questions.question: How soon does untreated Alchemical Grain rot?
questions.explanation: Untreated grain rots within two years.
